adjudication.adjudicator: NEW2 (single annotator), reading textHead for identity and textTail for the verdict
adjudication.method: Each row was judged against the DOCUMENT, never against the rule. textTail (last 900 chars) carries the disposal and the order; textHead (first 600) carries the identity of the proceeding. A row whose operative text is not in either window, or whose text is legacy-font mojibake, is `uncertain` and is excluded from the denominator rather than guessed.

decided.classNote: The errors are four families and none of them is a close call: disposal WITHOUT adjudication (infructuous, settlement, withdrawal, premature), NON-PROSECUTION, INTERLOCUTORY applications (condonation of delay), and BAIL orders. Bail leakage alone is 3 of 44 evaluable rows (6.8%) despite bail_order existing as its own class and scoring 100% itself.

decided_brief.classNote: This class is not a weaker version of `decided`; on this sample it is a different population wearing its name. 38 of 45 evaluable rows are withdrawals, dismissals for non-prosecution or default, condonation-of-delay applications, adjournments, restorations, or bail orders. The rule is `disposal_nature_merits_short`: the same merits-looking disposal string as `decided`, minus the length that gave the text room to disagree with it. Below roughly 1,500 characters the disposal string is carrying the whole decision and it is wrong most of the time.

bail_order.classNote: No errors. Every row is a bail, anticipatory-bail or bail-appeal matter. `text_bail_phrase` and `disposal_nature_bail` are both sound on this sample, which is what makes the bail leakage into `decided` a routing failure rather than a detection one.

procedural_disposal.classNote: One error in fifty, and it is instructive: the row was labelled from a registry code ("55-TRANSFER TO DEBT RECO.TRIBUNAL") that matches neither the text nor the outcome. The failure mode is the disposal vocabulary, not the rule.

reference_stub.classNote: No errors. Adjournments, listing orders, dispense-with orders, default dismissals, correction orders, and one document whose entire text is "1 2 3". `below_stub_length` is doing exactly what it claims.

pooled.note: The sample is STRATIFIED at 50 per class, so its own mix is not the corpus mix. These figures re-weight each class by its share of the CLASSIFIED corpus. A raw pooled rate over the 250 rows would flatter the result, because the two accurate classes are drawn at the same size as the two inaccurate ones.

decidedFamily.note: decided + decided_brief is the PRECEDENT-ELIGIBLE selector — what Tier A is built from. It is the number that matters and it is not the pooled one.

limits: ONE annotator, no second reader, no adjudication of disagreements — because there were none to have. Treat every figure as a single-rater estimate.

The windows are the last 900 and first 600 characters, which are not the document. A judgment whose operative order sits in the middle can be adjudicated wrongly from either end; those rows were marked uncertain where visible, and where not visible they are an unmeasured error in BOTH directions.

The draw is a contiguous primary-key run from a random start per class, not a uniform random sample. Neighbouring uuids share an insertion batch, so the effective sample size is smaller than 50 and the intervals here are optimistic.

Uncertain rows are excluded from the denominator. In `decided` 6 of 50 and in `decided_brief` 5 of 50 are legacy-font mojibake — 11 of 100 rows in the two Tier-A classes are documents nobody can read, which is a finding in its own right and not only a sampling nuisance.

The classes are judged against what the LABEL asserts. `decided` asserting a substantive final decision is the reading used here; if the intended meaning is looser, the precision is different and the definition, not the measurement, is what needs fixing.

caveats: Contiguous primary-key run from a random start, per class. Not a uniform random sample; adequate for finding defects, not for estimating a rate.

Classes are sampled at EQUAL size, so this is a stratified audit sample and its class mix is not the corpus mix. A per-class rate read off it is a rate WITHIN that class and pooling them without re-weighting by the corpus prior overstates the good classes.

textTail is the last 900 characters and textHead the first 600. Between them they are not the document: a judgment whose operative order sits in the middle, or whose tail is a signature block and a certificate, can be adjudicated wrongly from either end. Those rows are uncertain, not a guess.

such principal Civil Court, or any Court of
Small Causes;
(ii) in the case of international commercial
arbitration, the High Court in exercise of its
ordinary original civil jurisdiction, having
jurisdiction to decide the questions forming the
subject-matter of the arbitration if the same had
been the subject-matter of a suit, and in other
cases, a High Court having jurisdiction to hear
appeals from decrees of courts subordinate to
that High Court;”
3. The appropriate Court, in this case, would be
the Court of Principal Civil Court having the original
jurisdiction at Dehradun and not the High Court.
4. In view of the above, the writ petition fails and
it is hereby dismissed.

compassionate appointment

interested to pursue this petition and whether the order passed by this Court

TRA
Heard Mr. B. N. Majumder, learned counsel appearing for the claimant-petitioner as well as
Mr. J. Majumder, learned counsel appearing for the State-respondents.
By a common judgment and order dated 18.05.2015 the L.A. App. No.18 of 2009 and L.A.
App. No.19 of 2009 were dismissed.
The appellant-respondent has deposited for satisfying the award a sum of Rs.79,298/- in this
Registry by the cheque No.927112 dated 24.01.2017 on State Bank of India.
Now by this application, the claimant-petitioner has sought leave of this court for
withdrawing the said amount.
Mr J. Majumder, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-respondent does not oppose
such prayer.
Accordingly, Registry is directed to release the said amount to the claimant-petitioner,
namely Smt. Hangani Tripura following the procedure.
Accordingly, this petition stands allowed and disposed of.

ORDER
This is second application under section 439 Cr.P.C. arising out of crime
No. 196/2022 registered at P.S. Barod, district Agar for the offence punishable
under section 307 of IPC.
After going through the statement of victim recorded under section 161
Cr.P.C. and the medical report, it is found that 3 repeated blows of Darante
were given on chest. The injuries have been found to be dangerous to life.

accordingly dismissed.
